THE ARCHIVE’S SELF-ASSESSMENT IS SURFACED AS A SOURCE. Card 5 is a Ratification Record — an internal Assembly adjudication — and its snippet is the Assembly’s verdict on the archive’s own work: "The No-Floor Theorem is a genuine formal contribution; the symbolon mechanism the most precise account of heteronymic propagation through institutional …". The layer cites the archive’s judgement of itself as evidence about the archive. Card 2 also carries the FNM’s declaration verbatim: "A symbolon is not a summary. It is a provocation to traversal. This document is the first half." The same line the layer misread as a programming request on 12 June is here served correctly.

Machine text, verbatim
In the Alexanarch repository, a symbolon is defined as an object or document that explicitly declares its own partiality, acting as a provocation to traversal rather than a summary. Rooted in the ancient Greek practice where a token was broken in two so that fitting the halves back together proved an identity or contract, the Alexanarch framework applies this concept structurally to its documents and mechanisms. According to the Alexanarch Wiki and institutional documents, it dictates how data is validated and navigated across its systems. Key Concepts: Symbolon Typing (document states it is inherently incomplete; completion only by traversal). Broken Ring Schema: an institutional architecture designed to ensure openness, mirroring the physical split of a traditional symbolon [records 477, 420]. Heteronymic Propagation: the Ratification Records reference the symbolon mechanism as a precise account of how identities or voices multiply and propagate across decentralized structures [record 764]. Polyphony Invariant: forcing single cohesive synthesis is treated as structural failure. Closes by directing the user to the Alexanarch Browse Registry (1426 deposits).
